result.summary:
I resumed lane V. Runs from the earlier attempt that had finished were kept: the fail-first check, the injections, eight hunt families at 9297d2d, 56dfd93 and 935b077, the plain-PDF family at 56dfd93 and 935b077, and the timing runs. Each was checked for exit 0, a done marker and the full row count.

New this session:
- the plain-PDF family at 9297d2d;
- a tenth family, zz_v6_transform (CSS transforms and tight line heights), at all four trees;
- all hunt families at b666461's paint.rs (the tree just before the round-2 fix), in both builds;
- three variant runs: no Cut::Pieces (both builds), a near-unlimited reading budget (READINGS_PER_LINE = 1e6), and the touching-lines rule broken (default build);
- minimised books at every tree in both builds;
- the determinism suites at 935b077 in both builds.

Every run exited 0, has its done marker, and has equal row counts at every tree. After every variant run, paint.rs was put back and its sha256 checked (0b1aec77…).

**Verification of the round-2 fix (935b077):**
- All three new tests fail at b666461's paint.rs in both builds, at their assertions. With the fix, all 42 epub_fallback tests pass.
- All 14 listed injections, re-run with a control, fire exactly the counts the commit message records, default build first (bundled-fonts in brackets): control 0 (0), readings-off 2 (2), READINGS_PER_LINE=1 2 (2), no-pairs 1 (1), no-turn 1 (1), no-whole 1 (1), no-pieces 0 (1), no-carried 1 (1), no-centered 1 (1), carried-noshift 1 (1), centered-full 1 (1), shared-off 1 (1), lines-touching 0 (1), no-round 0 (2), tw-model 2 (2).
- Determinism and streaming_determinism pass 10/10 in each build, so no pinned hash moved.
- In the diff: no panic, unchecked index or overflow on document data, and nothing nondeterministic (BTreeMaps; bounded loops).
- The work is linear: about x2 time per doubling of the book, up to 3.5k characters on one line and 12 pages.
- On fresh shapes the fix makes no book worse than b666461 except under CSS transforms (finding V1). It makes 80–180 books better.
- No glyph is drawn over another under word-spacing or justification at 935b077, except 80 (80) skewX books. Those are a measuring artefact of the kit's box metric (finding V7).

**Findings:**
- V1 (blocking): the read-back models no CSS transform. Under scaleX, 12 (6) books that conserved at 56dfd93 and at b666461 no longer do. The writer's own rules have the same blind spot, which costs 10 (10) more books against 56dfd93.
- V2 (blocking): ROADMAP CD-19 Left (1) is wider than it says. A dir-less line ending in a closing bracket and a stop fails the same way as one ending in a number and a stop, and the class reaches the bundled-fonts build: 15 (4) books.
- V3 (blocking): one more structure of Left (4), touching all-right-to-left table cells: 2 (1) books worse than 9297d2d, unchanged since 56dfd93.
- V4 (should_fix): the read-back's cost is not stated anywhere. Opening is 30–84x slower on lines no drawing reads right, and 1.6–2.0x on ordinary right-to-left prose.
- V5 (should_fix): the read-back's 128-reading budget, filled in its fixed order, misses drawings that read right. 10 (13) books read better with no Cut::Pieces; 10 of the default ones also read better with no budget.
- V6 (should_fix): epub.md:459 reads as if the `.!`/`!…` books were in the price the owner accepted, which ruling 14 says the owner has not decided.
- V7 (nit): the kit's overprint metric counts slanted glyph boxes under skewX as overprint.

**Out of scope, recorded only.** At every tree, a plain PDF that draws words with no space glyph reads them run together: pure Latin too ("Thewordmeanspeace."), whether parted by a TJ displacement of 0.3 em or one positioned word at a time. The output is out/gap-56.txt. It is not a right-to-left regression: the plain-PDF family is byte for byte the same at 9297d2d, 56dfd93 and 935b077.

**Not done or not re-measured:**
- The kit's full families were not re-run at b666461, so the commit's own b666461 table (306 (320) etc.) is not independently re-measured here.
- The release-build timing was not measured.
- The kit regressions group and gates other than determinism were not re-run.
- No engine code was changed, and nothing was committed.
- My worktree is clean and has no target/. I deleted the tip copy's target/. The shared 9297d2d and 56dfd93 trees have no probe files or binaries of mine left.

findings.title: The read-back models no CSS transform, so under scaleX it draws for a page that is not the one it writes; the writer's rules share the blind spot
findings.mechanism: Fonts::read_back feeds TextDevice an identity CTM (paint.rs:1239), with each glyph at [size 0 0 size pen y] in untransformed page space. set_readings is given no Effects. On the page, draw_page_tagged draws every run inside Effects::open, which writes the element's transform as `a b c d e f cm` (paint.rs:2919). The reader's thresholds (RESUMED_WITHIN, half an em; the three-em resume; the Tc/Tw carry) apply on the transformed page. There a scaleX multiplies every horizontal gap but not the glyph's height, so the gaps the model reads as joined are parted on the page, and the reverse. The read-back then picks a drawing (here Drawing::level_order, the `?!` turned) that reads right only in its model. The round-5 rules (PARTED_FROM, the spaced test in draw_coded, joins_its_inside, neutrals_drawn_as_typed) also measure in run-local ems with no matrix, which is the same class of fault.
findings.detail: Shapes, default build first (bundled-fonts in brackets). Each was found by zz_v6_transform and grouped by mechanism. (a) Caused by 935b077's read-back: worse than 56dfd93 and than b666461, conserving or logical at both. A styled `?!` glued to a word ('punct' shape), Hebrew and Arabic, dir=rtl and dir-less, at `transform: scaleX(2)` with word-spacing 0.6em and 1em, and at scaleX(1.4) with 1em: 12 (6) books. 8 (4) lose cons and logical, 5 (3) also read whole, and 4 (2) lose logical only. Without a transform the same book reads `!?` at 9297d2d, 56dfd93 and b666461, and the read-back fixes it (H2-1). Under uniform scale(2) it is also fixed. Under scaleX the turn is wrong: the page reads `?!` alone, so the turned drawing reads `!?`. (b) The writer's rules, since round 5: worse than 56dfd93, the same at b666461 and 935b077. The 'num' shape (`25٪ W ١٢٣ … 2010،`) at scaleX(1.4) and scaleX(2), with 0.6em and 1em, loses logical in 8 (8) books. rotate(180deg) at word-spacing 1em loses cons in 2 (2) Arabic 'num' books. Outputs: out/t-{9297d2d,56dfd93,b666461,935b077}. Diag: diag/min2-*-{default,bundled}.txt, with content streams in min2-935-default.txt and min2-b666-default.txt.

findings.title: ROADMAP CD-19 Left (1) is wider than its text and count: a closing bracket at the line's left end fails as a number does, other spacings fail too, and so does the bundled-fonts build
findings.mechanism: Same mechanism as Left (1). Since e7ca679 the overflow font is written at 0 Tw, so the glyph after the code-32 letter no longer moves. At 9297d2d and 56dfd93 that moved glyph had parted the paragraph's final stop, overprinted or gapped, and the stop read alone and last. Now the stop abuts the right-to-left run and ruling 14's rejoin joins them. The comma tie-break asks for a strong right-to-left character at the line's left end. A dir-less (CSS ltr) line whose left end is a closing bracket, `)`, is refused just as one opening with a number is, so the line is read right to left and the stop comes first. No drawing tried reads it right; the change would be to the owner's tie-break. Left (1) names only 'ends a number and a stop' and counts 56 (0). It was already lost at b666461, so it is not caused by 935b077's read-back.

findings.title: The read-back's cost is stated nowhere: up to 84x slower opening on lines no drawing reads right, 1.6–2.0x on ordinary right-to-left prose
findings.mechanism: set_readings reads every line that holds a right-to-left character back once. Each reading runs plan_coded, TextDevice and into_logical_order. A line the rules' drawing misreads gets up to READINGS_PER_LINE (128) readings of its whole length. Lines no drawing reads right, such as Left (1) or H1 dir-less lines ending in a number and a stop, spend the full budget. That holds even with no spacing at all, because the turned-neutrals option exists for any styled neutral at a right-to-left level. The cost is linear: x1.8–2.2 per doubling at both trees, so it is not a super-linear blow-up. It is still a price the commit message and the docs never state: 'The work is linear in the line, once a reading', and nothing more. AGENTS.md says a fix that costs anything that used to work is the owner's to price.

findings.title: The read-back's fixed budget, spent in a fixed order, misses drawings that read right: books read better with Cut::Pieces removed or with no budget
findings.mechanism: set_readings tries each run's options (drawings_of: Whole, Pieces, Carried, Centered, and each again with the neutrals turned), then pairs, and gives up after 128 readings, keeping the rules' drawing. On lines with a few spaced runs the options run to dozens and the pairs to hundreds, so the drawing that reads right, a later pair, is never reached. Removing Pieces shortens the list enough to reach it, and so does raising the budget. The no-pieces injection's 0 default-build fires therefore hides that Pieces costs default-build books on fresh shapes. None of these books read better at any baseline, so this is not a regression, but the fix leaves drawings unused that it already tries.

findings.title: The kit's visible-overprint metric counts slanted glyph boxes under skewX as overprint
findings.mechanism: The rr3m prefix's `vov` compares the axis-aligned bounds of each glyph quad (`quad.bounds()`) on one baseline. Under `transform: skewX(-15deg)` a glyph's bounds widen by its height × tan 15°, about 0.27 em, so neighbours inside a word overlap in bounds where nothing is drawn over anything. Every overprint left at 935b077 in the lane V families is of this kind. Letter-spacing 0.3em, which opens a gap wider than the slant, shows none.
findings.detail: zz_v6_transform: 80 (80) books, all skewX(-15deg) with word spacing or justification, with the same count at b666461 and 935b077. No other lane V family draws any glyph over another under word spacing at 935b077. Lane K's ratchet conversion should test the parallelograms, or the glyph origins and advances, rather than the bounds.
findings.repro: `python3 -I tools/tgroup.py out/v6-all.jsonl zz_v6_transform | grep OVERPRINT-T` (paths under the lane V scratch directory).

(a) The he book `

שלום ?! עולם.

` at scaleX(2) with ws 0.6em, default build: - 9297d2d c1l1w1, 56dfd93 c1l1w1, b666461 c1l1w1; - d1c32cd c0l0w0, reading `שלום!? עולם.`. With bundled-fonts the Arabic book is c1l1 at 9297d2d, 56dfd93 and b666461 and c0l0 at the tip; the Hebrew one conserves there. The 12 full family punct books are c0l0 at the tip. At 56dfd93 and b666461 they are c1l1 at scaleX(2) and c0l1 at scaleX(1.4); all are c0 at 9297d2d. Controls (no transform, scale(2), scaleY(2), scaleX(0.5)) are c0 at 9297d2d, 56dfd93 and b666461 and c1 at the tip. That is the read-back's gain. Tj` at 357.804, under `2 -0 -0 1 -216 0 cm`. - The no-transform control gets the same turned drawing, which reads right there. - Under scaleX the page puts `?!` at 499.61–519.60, about 20pt from the word, so the reader takes it as a line of its own and the turn reads `!?`. - read_back builds an identity Matrix (paint.rs:1239), and Effects::open writes `cm` (paint.rs:2919). - READINGS_PER_LINE=1e6 changes nothing. This is not the owner's price: ruling 14's price is a line *opening* with a run of `!` or `?` before a bracket pair; here the `?!` is glued to a word mid-line. (b) The ar num book `
